s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic inflammatory condition of the nails and mucosa with potential systemic involvement
salient_findings: Painful swelling of the proximal nail folds
Dripping of blood from fingernails and toenails
Lichenoid plaques and erosions on the oral mucosa
Violaceous discoloration and longitudinal ridging of the nails
Raised liver enzyme levels and positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Symptoms present for the last year
No history of preceding trauma or drug intake
Proximal nail folds are swollen and show violaceous discoloration
Nails demonstrate longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation
Partial to complete loss of nail plate with oozing of blood and hemorrhagic crusting
Oral mucosa shows lichenoid plaques and erosions
Raised liver enzyme levels
Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status
Histopathology shows hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, acanthosis, and basal cell degeneration
Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis

shortlist.label: Lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation of swollen proximal nail folds, violaceous discoloration, and oral mucosa lichenoid plaques and erosions are consistent with lichen planus

shortlist.label: Hepatitis C-associated lichen planus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and clinical presentation of lichen planus-like symptoms suggest a possible association between hepatitis C and lichen planus

shortlist.label: Psoriatic nail disease
shortlist.why_kept: Nail changes such as longitudinal ridging, thinning, and focal fragmentation are consistent with psoriatic nail disease, although other symptoms are more suggestive of lichen planus

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Dense bandlike lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in the papillary dermis and basal cell degeneration are consistent with dermatomyositis, although other symptoms are more suggestive of lichen planus

shortlist.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
shortlist.why_kept: Association with hepatitis C and clinical presentation of painful swelling of the proximal nail folds and erosions on the oral mucosa are consistent with necrolytic acral erythema

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including painful swelling of the proximal nail folds, lichenoid plaques on the oral mucosa, and histopathological findings of hyperkeratosis, hypergranulosis, and basal cell degeneration, are consistent with lichen planus. Additionally, the patient's positive anti-hepatitis C virus antibody status and raised liver enzyme levels support the association with hepatitis C.

rejected.label: Lichen planus
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with lichen planus, the presence of hepatitis C infection suggests a specific subtype.

rejected.label: Psoriatic nail disease
rejected.why: The patient's nail findings, such as longitudinal ridging and thinning, are not typical of psoriatic nail disease, which usually presents with pitting, onycholysis, and subungual hyperkeratosis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of dermatomyositis, which typically presents with Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash, and muscle weakness.

rejected.label: Necrolytic acral erythema
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings do not support a diagnosis of necrolytic acral erythema, which typically presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques on the feet and hands, and is often associated with hepatitis C infection, but the clinical presentation is distinct from the patient's symptoms.
